title: The Doubling Rule
rule: When a short word has one short vowel and ends in one consonant, and the ending starts with a vowel (ing, ed, er, est), double the last letter: hop becomes hopping.
trickText: Check three things. One short vowel? Ends in one consonant? Does the ending start with a vowel? Then double the last letter. If not, just add the ending.
say: Today's case: the doubling rule. When a short word has one short vowel and ends in one consonant, and the ending starts with a vowel, we double the last letter. Hop plus i n g makes hopping, with two p's.

activities.instruction: Do you double the last letter, or just add the ending?

categories.label: Double the last letter
categories.why: One short vowel, one ending consonant, and a vowel ending: double the last letter.

categories.label: Just add the ending
categories.why: No doubling needed: just add the ending.
